compile_track.locus: _resolve_sources 9810-9836 (globs ALL fused TUs); dispatch-table coupling comment 9815-9826
compile_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: _resolve_sources at 9830-9835 sorted(fused_dir.iterdir()) globs every mega_<model>_<opt> TU unconditionally for every build; 4 megakernel model TUs linked into every single-cell .so.
compile_track.description: Scope the fused-TU set to the tuned cell only; precompile the other 3 model megakernels to .o once and link via prebuilt-.o index, turning a 4-megakernel AOT build into a 1-megakernel build.
compile_track.mechanism: Comment at 9815-9826 documents the HARD CONSTRAINT this must respect: fused_dispatch_table.inc references EVERY mega_<model>_<opt> symbol unconditionally, so naive source-dropping fails at dlopen ('undefined symbol: sg::fused::sm90::mega_…'). The candidate's prebuilt-.o link path is the correct workaround — populate spec with bindings+launchers+models+[current-cell megakernel], link the 3 non-tuned megakernel .o files via spec.ldflags. _plan_incremental_build already reuses AOT .o for unchanged TUs, so the plumbing exists.
compile_track.expected_effect: AOT build 60-75% faster for single-cell sweeps (~4x source reduction). JIT variant builds unaffected.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: dlopen symbol resolution preserved for ALL 4 cells (the dispatch-table symbols must all still resolve); measured AOT wall-clock with full sweep.
compile_track.note: Highest-value compile item: directly attacks the 4x-redundant-megakernel-link that every single-cell build pays. The dispatch-table symbol coupling (9815-9826) is the real engineering risk and the candidate correctly addresses it.

compile_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: TODO at 14383 states the variant timer compiles each .so SERIALLY inline in the closure and 'the compile — not the timing — dominates wall-clock'.
compile_track.description: ProcessPoolExecutor to pre-compile the next K candidate variants in parallel while the GPU times the current variant, overlapping I/O-bound compile with timing.
compile_track.mechanism: The author's own TODO (14383-14392) names this as a 'large speedup' but explicitly defers it: 'touches cache-write concurrency, the TimingWorker handshake, and ninja-build-dir isolation … intentionally NOT attempted … Do not half-wire a pool here.' So the mechanism is real but the three named hazards (per-variant ninja build-dir isolation to avoid .o collisions, cache-write races, worker handshake) MUST be solved together.
compile_track.expected_effect: 20-35% wall-clock reduction on Bayesian/Exhaustive sweeps where compile dominates, scaling with NCPUS.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: no variant .so collision/corruption (ninja-dir isolation); reproducibility (same trial sequence → same winners); measured full-sweep wall-clock.
compile_track.note: High ceiling, but the author flagged the exact integration hazards — needs the cache-concurrency + ninja-isolation done as one piece, not incrementally.

compile_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: the numeric feature tuple exists at 5103+ with the listed hand-engineered features; FEATURE_DIM is computed at 5158.
compile_track.description: Add tile_m/tile_n coverage, occupancy-vs-regpressure Pareto, ILP proxy, mem-bw/flops ratio, and interaction terms (block×maxrregcount); retrain from existing sidecar trial data.
compile_track.mechanism: Expand featurize_config + _COST_MODEL_NUMERIC_FEATURES + FEATURE_DIM; rescore historical trials from the .jsonl sidecars. Better cost-model MAE → better multi-fidelity/absolute-threshold pruning in the variant timer.
compile_track.expected_effect: Cost-model MAE 15-25% lower → 10-20% better pruning accuracy; indirect sweep-time win scaling with pruned-trial count.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: feature computation sound; cost-model MAE on historical trials; ablation old-vs-new features.

compile_track.locus: ss_prefilter rule parse 2911-2950; compile_feasibility_check 3091-3093 (rules compiled into a list per call)
compile_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: rules eval left-to-right (3098 loop over compiled list in YAML order); 3092-3093 compiles them once per check.
compile_track.description: Reorder prefilter rules by elimination ratio (highest-rejection first) measured on a config sample; optional dominance short-circuit.
compile_track.mechanism: Add a rule-optimization pass that measures per-rule elimination ratio on a ~1000-config sample (or historical data), reorders the compiled list so the most-eliminating rule runs first → average-case short-circuit. The 'byte-identical survivor set' gate makes reordering provably safe (AND-of-rules is order-independent for the result, only for cost).
compile_track.expected_effect: 30-60% fewer rule evals per config on tight rule sets; 5-10% faster sweep initialization at large Cartesian sizes.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: prefiltered survivor set byte-identical before/after reorder; measured prefilter wall-clock on large config sets.
compile_track.note: Genuinely new (the compile() caching half of the original claim is already done at 3092). Reordering is the live part; the byte-identical-survivor gate makes it safe.

compile_track.grounded: PARTIALLY: bias_trial_queue / STALL_DIM_HINTS plumbing exists (6385-6400); the cold-start n_startup_trials is structure-agnostic.
compile_track.description: Seed TPE startup with cost-model-ranked feasible configs (re-rank the feasible set by predicted ms before study.ask) and warm-start Parzen estimators from prior d=128 runs (cross-depth transfer).
compile_track.mechanism: Extend bias_trial_queue to enqueue top-K cost-model-predicted configs in addition to stall-hints; add a re-ranking phase before study.ask() filtering by cost-model decile. Transfer: reuse a cached cost_model for the same (opt,model,arch,vendor) at another depth as a feature-weight prior. Subsumes compile-09's startup-feasibility-pass (register-feasible startup configs) — merge the two: rank by predicted-ms AND filter infeasible-register configs in one warm-start pass.
compile_track.expected_effect: Startup (first 50-100 trials) 20-35% faster convergence; 10-15% overall on mid budgets; infeasible-trial rate drops (compile-09 contribution).
compile_track.gate: Self-test: startup configs feasible + correctly ranked; convergence metric (time-to-top-K) vs baseline TPE.
compile_track.note: DEDUP: absorbs compile-09 (megakernel-tile startup-feasibility-pass) — both bias TPE startup; compile-09's register-feasibility filter becomes the feasibility leg of this candidate's warm-start.

compile_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: the accumulator memoizes (n_trials,best_ms); the proposal extends it to cache per-trial feature vectors + predictions.
compile_track.description: Cache per-trial feature vectors and cost-model predictions in the sidecar accumulator so cost-model retrain on reload skips recomputing features for the full history.
compile_track.mechanism: Extend _SIDECAR_SUMMARY_ACCUM to store feature_cache/predicted_cache keyed by config_key; record_trial computes+caches once on append; retrain reuses cached features.
compile_track.expected_effect: Cost-model retrain at Bayesian startup 20-40% faster for long-running experiments (feature recompute ~30% of train time).
compile_track.gate: Self-test: feature-cache consistency across sidecar reload; measured retrain time.
compile_track.note: Synergistic with compile-04 (expanded features make caching them more valuable).

compile_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE but UNVERIFIED soundness: claims the cicc→ptxas device pass is deterministic w.r.t. (source,flags) and thus cacheable like sccache.
compile_track.description: Hash-keyed object cache around the nvcc device passes (cicc→ptxas) keyed on (TU source + device flags + device macro set), linking cached .o on hit.
compile_track.mechanism: Instrument _torch_load to capture the device-compile command line; pre-hash; check a local .o cache; populate on miss. SOUNDNESS RISK: ptxas output is NOT guaranteed bit-reproducible across all flag combos and toolkit builds; the cache must key on the EXACT nvcc/ptxas version + every -D that reaches device code (overlaps the COMPILE_PY_BUILD_CACHE_HOIST audit). If sccache already wraps the host pass, the marginal win is only the device pass.
compile_track.expected_effect: Author estimates 30-50% per-variant build-time on 60-75% hit rate after warmup; contingent on device-pass reproducibility holding.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: device .o binary equivalence under full rebuild (the make-or-break check); measured per-variant build time.
compile_track.note: DEDUP: COMPILE_PY_BUILD_CACHE_HOIST (root compile.py, non-existent file) folds in here as the cache-key-completeness audit (verify ALL SG_TUNED_* device macros participate in the key) — that audit is the correctness prerequisite for this cache to be sound.

compile_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: AOT cache key = H(sources,flags,search_space,pgo); a tuned-macro build with the same source set could in principle alias the AOT entry.
compile_track.description: Fold a hash of the tuned-macro set into the AOT cache key (or separate aot_primary vs aot_tuned entries) to prevent a tuned-macro .so aliasing the no-macro AOT .so.
compile_track.mechanism: _hash_sources optionally takes variant_id; when spec carries tuned macros, fold them into the AOT key. Correctness/reliability gain (eliminates a rare stale-.so reuse); negligible timing.
compile_track.expected_effect: Eliminates a latent incorrect-cache-hit class; no perf change.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: macro'd vs no-macro AOT entries never collide; prior tuned configs + new sweeps don't step on each other.
compile_track.note: DEDUP: this IS the concrete fix the COMPILE_PY_BUILD_CACHE_HOIST audit (rank-7 note) would recommend; pair them.

compile_track.grounded: PARTIAL: prefilter rules already compiled once per check-call (3092); the cross-sweep memo + cached iterdir + batched report-writes are the residual.
compile_track.description: Hoist prefilter compile() to a sweep-level cache, cache sorted(fused_dir.iterdir()) with mtime-watch, batch report.write into a deferred-flush buffer.
compile_track.mechanism: Memoize the compiled-rule list across the whole sweep (not just per check-call); cache the fused TU Path list keyed (arch,mtime); flush report writes once per Bayesian iteration.
compile_track.expected_effect: 2-5ms host latency per trial → 1-2% wall-clock at large budgets.
compile_track.gate: Self-test: prefilter output identical; pure-caching, no functional change.
compile_track.note: Lowest compile-track value; the prefilter-compile leg is largely already done. Synergizes with compile-01 (the iterdir cache) and compile-05 (the rule list).

model_track.locus: Split-K dW machinery 1576-1592; tunable kDecDwSplitK 93-95,120-121 (default 4, static_assert >=1 only)
model_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: Split-K with DETERMINISTIC ascending-chunk reduce (no float atomics, fixed order) at 1576-1592; G==1 routes to single-CTA path; comment documents ~62% idle SMs in P2 (50 dW tiles / 132 SMs).
model_track.description: Raise SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK from 4 toward 8 (or grid-adaptive) to fill the ~62% idle SMs in P2 dW; floor-balanced partition guarantees no empty chunks.
model_track.mechanism: Each (output_tile,chunk) is a work item; more chunks → fuller occupancy. The partial-reduce is O(1)/chunk via the deterministic ascending-chunk sum → PARITY + A/A/A preserved BY CONSTRUCTION (the candidate is bit-neutral). Constraint: dw_part scratch scales linearly with G (offset formula at 1587); must validate against the documented 62 MB workspace headroom.
model_track.expected_effect: 10-20% P2 wall-clock at d=2048 by raising dW occupancy from ~38% toward 60%+. P2 dW is the documented post-H2 bottleneck.
model_track.gate: Kernel: fp64 parity + ascending-chunk-sum determinism bit-identical to G=1; 3-seed timing at d=2048 with G in {4,6,8}; workspace-memory bounds validation.
model_track.note: FLAGSHIP MODEL ITEM: bit-neutral by construction (deterministic reduce), attacks the single largest documented d=2048 inefficiency (62% idle SMs in P2), gated only by a pure tunable bump + workspace headroom. Highest gain×confidence/risk in the whole set. UNLIKE the swizzle and S=3 items, kDecDwSplitK has NO blocking static_assert (only >=1).

model_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: kIL=min(MaxAtomsM,kDecMaxIL); interleave issues kIL wgmmas/k-step into independent WgmmaAccum<N> acc[kIL] sharing one B-tile (503,524-531); static_assert allows up to 4.
model_track.description: Expand dW M-atom interleave width from 2 to 4 for large-Nout dW tiles (ff0 [512,128], ff2 [128,512]) to deepen tensor-pipe MMA overlap while keeping B-staging constant.
model_track.mechanism: k-step issues kIL back-to-back wgmmas into independent fp32 accumulators; per-atom accumulation stays ASCENDING-k (k=0 overwrite, k>0 add) → bit-identical numerics + A/A/A unchanged (comment 497-499). Cost: 4×(N/2) fp32 accumulator regs per thread + 4 A-tiles/slot smem — the smem is pre-sized for kAtomsM=production-max and the static_assert already permits 4. Best delivered via BEHAVIOR-003 (per-orientation IL) so fwd/dX stay at the proven 2 and only dW goes to 4.
model_track.expected_effect: 15-25% dW K-loop reduction for Nout>=256 via tensor-pipe saturation; marginal for small Nout.
model_track.gate: Kernel: fp64 parity (ascending-k per atom); 3-seed timing on ff0/ff2 dW tiles at d=2048; register-spill check (PTX -v) that 4×(N/2) accumulators don't spill.
model_track.note: DEDUP: subsumes BEHAVIOR-003-ATOM-INTERLEAVE-WIDTH-CONFIG (per-GEMM IL tunable) and IL_LOOP_UNROLL_AND_PIPELINING — all three are the same interleave-width lever. BEHAVIOR-003's per-orientation split is the SAFE delivery vehicle (keeps fwd/dX at 2). Register-spill at IL=4 is the real gate.

model_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: G is currently a compile-time #define; the deterministic reduce works for any G.
model_track.description: Make G adaptive at launch: G = clamp(max(4, nCTA/dW_tile_count), workspace-bound) so one compiled kernel adapts to GPU count / batch size without recompile.
model_track.mechanism: Device-side dectc_dw_splitk_adaptive(nCTA, dW_tile_count) returns G; minor kernel-signature change to accept G as a runtime param instead of #define. Determinism holds for any G (ascending-chunk sum).
model_track.expected_effect: Same occupancy boost as PERF-004 but auto-tuned across launch shapes; no recompile per shape.
model_track.gate: Kernel: fp64 parity + workspace bounds validation for G up to 8.
model_track.note: Natural follow-on to flagship PERF-004: PERF-004 finds the best static G, BEHAVIOR-002 makes it shape-adaptive. Sequence them (static first, then adaptive).

model_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: head loops over kVocab with per-thread scatter + early-exit (o<kVocab) at small Vocab.
model_track.description: Tile the vocab loop (e.g. 32-output blocks/thread) in head CE fwd AND cache out_w in smem for the head-bwd dhn contraction (VIT_TC_008), eliminating per-sample 97-weight rescans.
model_track.mechanism: Block the vocab loop to cut warp-divergent early-exit + L1 thrash; stage out_w [kD×kVocab ~50KB] into smem once per block so the dhn=Σ_o dlogits·out_w contraction reads smem not gmem. Numerics unchanged (same reduction, same order).
model_track.expected_effect: 2-5% head CE fwd + 3-5% head bwd; both P1-head and P1-bwd-head benefit.
model_track.gate: Kernel: bit-identical logits/softmax/loss + dhn; 3-seed timing at d=2048; head clock64 delta if SG_VIT_PROFILE.
model_track.note: DEDUP: merges VIT_TC_001 (fwd vocab tiling) + VIT_TC_008 (bwd out_w smem cache) + VIT_TC_013 (warp-per-sample) — all target the same head-CE per-sample/per-vocab inefficiency. 50KB smem for out_w must be checked against the kernel's existing ~42KB static budget (occupancy assert at fused_decoder 317).

model_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: the ViT GEMM engine mirrors the decoder interleave (#pragma unroll 1 on the group loop, one group at a time).
model_track.description: Software-pipeline the ViT GEMM group loop: issue group g's MMAs, then stage group g+1's B-tile during g's wgmma_wait, overlapping stage latency with compute.
model_track.mechanism: Restructure the g0 loop as a classic prologue/steady pipeline (the same pattern the decoder cp.async ring already uses). Accumulation order unchanged (ascending-k per atom) → bit-identical. Applies to fwd/dX/dW call sites.
model_track.expected_effect: 2-4% per call site; cumulative ~3-4% across P1+P2.
model_track.gate: Kernel: fp64 parity (ascending-k preserved); 3-seed timing at d=2048.
model_track.note: DEDUP: merges VIT_TC_010 + VIT_TC_018 (both pipeline the ViT M-atom interleave) + VIT_TC_011 (P1 tile-loop unroll, weaker variant). This is the decoder PERF-005 idea ported to ViT; once the decoder interleave-width work lands, port the winning structure here.

model_track.locus: LN fwd 572-585 (mean-loop+vit_block_sum, then var-loop+vit_block_sum); LN bwd 593-621
model_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: lines 572-577 do TWO block reductions (mean then variance) with the variance loop reading (xr[j]-mean) — a genuine two-pass.
model_track.description: Reduce LN sync/reduction count by merging the dgamma/dbeta + sda/sdax passes in LN BWD (NOT the fwd mean/var, which cannot be single-passed without breaking numerics).
model_track.mechanism: SCOPED DOWN from the original (fwd fusion is parity-unsafe — see dropped note): the LN-bwd fusion at 597-620 combines the dgw/dgb accumulation loop with the sda/sdax loop under a single owner-per-j rule, cutting __syncthreads from ~5 to 2-3 WITHOUT changing accumulation order. The fwd two-pass variance MUST stay two-pass (Σ(x-mean)² needs mean first; sum/sumsq fusion changes rounding).
model_track.expected_effect: 2-4% LN bwd (runs 2×/layer); decoder LN has identical shape (dual win).
model_track.gate: Kernel: deterministic single-owner-per-j accumulation, numerics bit-identical; 3-seed timing.
model_track.note: DEDUP+SCOPE: VIT_TC_002 (fwd) + VIT_TC_003 (bwd) merged; the FWD-fusion half is DROPPED for parity (Σ(x-mean)² is inherently two-pass), only the BWD sync-merge survives and only the sync-count, not accumulation, may change.

model_track.locus: patch_proj input staging 700-706 (float->bf16) then smem stage 711-728 with a __syncthreads between
model_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: two cooperative loops + a sync; the candidate's own size estimate was self-corrected to ~3% of GEMM volume.
model_track.description: Fuse the float->bf16 patch conversion with the Major-K smem staging into one stage_kmajor_tile pass, saving one __syncthreads and improving L1 locality.
model_track.mechanism: stage_kmajor_tile reads float patches, converts inline, writes Major-K in one pass. bf16 conversion bit-identical.
model_track.expected_effect: ~1% (patch_proj is a small fraction of token-GEMM volume).
model_track.gate: Kernel: bf16 conversion identical, zero numeric change; 3-seed timing.
model_track.note: Small but clean and bit-neutral. The original's own size correction (94%→3%) is the honest figure.

model_track.locus: P3 apply_optimizer dispatch 1098-1099; per-element adamw bc1/bc2
model_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: maps onto the same per-element-vs-per-tensor scalar question as the decoder elemwise track; bc1/bc2 broadcast.
model_track.description: Broadcast bc1=1-b1^step, bc2=1-b2^step (and Muon/SG aux variants) once per CTA in smem before the P3 tensor loop, instead of recomputing the powf per dispatch.
model_track.mechanism: Compute the powers once into __shared__ with one __syncthreads, pass to apply_optimizer. Same powf math, reordered → bit-identical.
model_track.expected_effect: 2-4% P3 (fewer fp32 powf + better I-cache reuse) across optimizers.
model_track.gate: Kernel: math identical (same powf, hoisted); 3-seed timing at d=2048.
model_track.note: NOTE the decoder twin already hoists Muon aux bc1/bc2 to per-TENSOR (fused_decoder 1297-1298) — verify whether ViT P3 actually recomputes per-element before investing; if the compiler already hoists the loop-invariant powf, this is a no-op. Cross-track sibling of elemwise-002/elemwise-015.

optimizer_track.locus: adamw_step 30-62, adamw_step_vec4 65-105 (EXISTS, hand-written, never called); P3 loop fused_decoder 288-289
optimizer_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: adamw_step_vec4 is fully implemented at 65-105 but the P3 loop (fused_decoder 288-289) calls per-element apply_optimizer<Opt>; the vec4 path is dead.
optimizer_track.description: Wire the existing vec4 fast-path into the P3 tail for FP32 AdamW(-tail) optimizers, gated on per-tensor size%4==0, processing 4 elements/call.
optimizer_track.mechanism: P3 loop at 288 calls apply_optimizer<Opt> scalar; for the AdamW branch (opt_components 386) route a size%4==0 aligned tensor through adamw_step_vec4. Bulk float4 load/store of (param,exp_avg,exp_avg_sq,grad) cuts L1 bandwidth 4x and relieves register pressure (P3 runs near the 200-reg threshold). Math is bit-identical (same per-lane FLOPs, same order). REALITY: only the AdamW/SG2-tail branch has a vec4 today; extending to the 9 other branches is more work, so scope v1 to AdamW + SG2-tail.
optimizer_track.expected_effect: 2-4% at d=2048 from reduced L1 misses + register relief on large tensors; neutral on the few <256-elem tensors.
optimizer_track.gate: fp64 parity hard-gate (vec4 is bit-identical math) + 3-seed timing at d=2048.
optimizer_track.note: FLAGSHIP OPTIMIZER ITEM: the vec4 kernel is ALREADY WRITTEN and validated-shaped (adamw.h:65-105) but unused — lowest-effort/highest-certainty win in the track. Bit-identical by construction. The decoder tensors at d=2048 are large enough (ff0/ff2 65536 elems) to bite.

optimizer_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: P3 was never autotuned (the search space targets the GEMM tile/IL/stages, not the optimizer tail).
optimizer_track.description: Add P3-specific autotune knobs: {vec_width:{1,2,4}, smem_scalar_cache:{off,on}, small-tensor batch threshold} and tune on live steps.
optimizer_track.mechanism: Orthogonal P3 search dimension; generate specializations, autotune, pick winner. This is the systematic vehicle that MEASURES elemwise-001 (vec_width), elemwise-013 (batch threshold), elemwise-015 (smem scalar cache) rather than hand-guessing them.
optimizer_track.expected_effect: 1-3% if the current scalar/no-cache default is sub-optimal (likely, since P3 is untuned); +2-3x compile time per cell for the extra configs.
optimizer_track.gate: 3-seed timing at d=2048 for top-K winners vs baseline.
optimizer_track.note: DEDUP/UMBRELLA: this is the autotune harness that turns elemwise-001/013/015 from guesses into measured wins. Sequence: land elemwise-001 (vec4) first as a proven default, then let this knob explore the rest.

optimizer_track.locus: FusedOptState struct 105-243 (300+ bytes, interleaved null pointers)
optimizer_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: FusedOptState (105-243) is a large struct with shared Adam scalars interleaved among many optimizer-specific pointers (psi_*, sam_dir, orth, s_track, smart_grad…).
optimizer_track.description: Reorder FusedOptState to pack the hot shared Adam scalars (lr,beta1,beta2,eps,wd,bc1,bc2) into the first cache line; push rarely-touched per-optimizer pointers later.
optimizer_track.mechanism: apply_optimizer's hot path reads only the shared scalars; grouping them into one 64B line reduces cache-line bouncing across the P3 element loop. No semantic change (field reorder only).
optimizer_track.expected_effect: <1% standalone; 3-5% combined with elemwise-001 (vec4) + the sg2-001 scalar-prefetch family (reduced cache-line traffic compounds).
optimizer_track.gate: fp64 parity hard-gate (pure field reorder) + 3-seed timing.
optimizer_track.note: DEDUP: pairs with sg2-001 (cache per-tensor scalars in regs at stage entry) — both reduce per-element scalar-load traffic; same theme as elemwise-015 (smem scalar cache) and elemwise-018 (__restrict__). Land as a small bundle.

optimizer_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: 1210-1218 writes g_sorted/s_sorted into ws.q then 1224-1227 copies to ws.win_k/win_v — two full-N passes + two syncs; the author's own comment (1220-1223) shows they considered strided views and chose the copy for simplicity.
optimizer_track.description: Compute g_sorted/s_sorted on-the-fly in GRU/PEER via perm indirection (grad[perm[r]], sharp[perm[r]]) instead of materializing through ws.q then copying.
optimizer_track.mechanism: Remove 1210-1227; pass perm+grad+sharp into sg2_stage_gru/peer which gather inline. Saves 2×(N·sizeof(float)) HBM writes + 2 CTA-wide syncs. PARITY: the gather order must be byte-identical to the current materialized order (same perm[r] map) — the comment confirms GRU/PEER already read grad[perm[r]], so the math is unchanged, only the staging is removed.
optimizer_track.expected_effect: For large N saves ~800KB writes + 2 syncs/tensor; small absolute but real on the SG2 cell's hottest tensors.
optimizer_track.gate: compile.py self-test + fp64 parity (GRU/PEER logic unchanged, indexing shift only); 3-seed timing across mixed N at d=2048.
optimizer_track.note: Best-grounded SG2 item: the two-pass+two-sync is right there at 1207-1230 and the author flagged it as a simplicity-over-perf choice that this candidate reverses. SG2 is the HCA/CSA NSA meta-optimizer — parity gate is the d-estimate/loss trajectory.

optimizer_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: the head_dim inner loop unrolls but the outer Nh loop (small, 2-8 for typical N) does not.
optimizer_track.description: Add #pragma unroll 2/4 on the HCA dense-attention Nh loop to expose ILP across the online-softmax accumulation.
optimizer_track.mechanism: Nh<=N/HCA_COMPRESS is small; unrolling the outer loop pipelines the online-softmax reductions. Same math (online-softmax is associative-stable in this fixed order) → bit-identical.
optimizer_track.expected_effect: 5-10% on the HCA attention stage (~40% of S2).
optimizer_track.gate: compile.py: numerical equivalence; measure HCA attention stage latency at d=2048.
optimizer_track.note: Cleanest pure-perf SG2 micro: a pragma on a small loop, no layout/order change. Cross-track sibling of the decoder/ViT interleave-pipelining theme.

optimizer_track.grounded: PLAUSIBLE: GRU_HIDDEN=4 default means one float4 per element — a natural vec4 boundary for the state load/store.
optimizer_track.description: Vectorize gru_state load/store as float4 (GRU_HIDDEN=4 → exactly one float4/element), coalescing into 4x-wider transactions.
optimizer_track.mechanism: Replace scalar gru_state reads/writes with float4; __ldg on reads. Same I/O, vectorized → bit-identical. NOTE this collides with sg2-006 (gru_state scatter reorder) — they touch the same writes; pick vectorization (lower risk) over the scatter-reorder unless profiling shows scatter is the dominant stall.
optimizer_track.gate: compile.py: numerical equivalence (vectorized I/O); measure GRU state I/O bandwidth at d=2048.
optimizer_track.note: DEDUP: supersedes sg2-006 (scatter-opt) for the same gru_state writes — vec4 is the lower-risk lever; only pursue sg2-006 if vec4 leaves a measured scatter stall.

optimizer_track.grounded: CONFIRMED: sc.alpha[tid]/beta1[tid]/gru_decay[tid]/lamb_eff[tid]/bc1[tid]/bc2[tid] are indexed at the apply call (1245-1247).
optimizer_track.description: Cache the 6 per-tensor scalars into registers at sg2_meta_stages entry instead of re-indexing by tid per stage.

dropped.reason: PARITY-RISK + FALSE MECHANISM. Claims 'enable kSwizzle128B, no numerics change, only descriptor bits 63:62 differ.' GROUND TRUTH (wgmma.cuh 250-288 + staging 584-594): the descriptor LBO/SBO (lbo=MN*16, sbo=128) and the smem staging map (half*(MN*8)+mn*8) are derived SPECIFICALLY for the NONE/INTERLEAVE layout. 128B swizzle requires a DIFFERENT smem tile layout AND different LBO/SBO; flipping only the swizzle bits makes the wgmma read garbage. The 'zero-copy' claim is false. The substrate supports the modes for the self-test, but production GEMM would need a full re-stage + re-derived descriptors — not the bit-neutral edit claimed.

DUPLICATE of WGMMA_SMEM_BANK_SWIZZLE; same false 'zero-copy descriptor change' premise. Same parity-risk: the staging loop (model_stage_decoder_tc 584-594) writes the NONE-layout interleave; 128B swizzle needs a different write map + LBO/SBO. Dropped for the same reason.

Tunable wrapper for the swizzle change that is itself parity-unsafe in production. Exposing -DSG_TUNED_WGMMA_SWIZZLE doesn't make 128B correct without re-staging + re-deriving LBO/SBO (wgmma.cuh 250-288). The substrate template param exists; the model-header staging does not produce a swizzled layout. Dropped: would compile and silently corrupt the GEMM.

PARITY/CORRECTNESS-RISK. The cp.async ring (model_stage_decoder_tc 607-628) issues cp_async_wait_group<0>+fence_async_proxy+__syncthreads per k-iter to publish the slot before its first wgmma read; the comment (545-551,617-619) documents this as the silicon-validated tile_pipeline handshake with WAR-safety on slot (k+1)%S. Moving the async-proxy fence outside the loop breaks the gmem->smem visibility ordering the wgmma depends on — a memory-ordering hazard, not a free micro-op. The 1-2% claim is not worth risking the validated handshake.

BLOCKED BY DESIGN INVARIANT + not a free bump. kDecTcStages is hard static_assert'd <=2 (model_stage_decoder_tc 116-117: 'must be 1 or 2'); S=3 requires lifting the assert AND redesigning the 2-slot WAR-safety (slot drained at k-1, released at k). The S=2 double-buffer is the already-validated mamba-TC carryover (comment 82-89). S=3 is real ring-buffer rework with smem growth, not the tunable bump the candidate implies.

DUPLICATE of RING_DEPTH_INCREASE_S3 (both need S>=3). Same static_assert<=2 wall (116-117) and same 3-slot WAR-safety redesign + smem/register growth. The 5-10% ceiling is real but the candidate misframes it as a tunable; it is a ring rewrite gated by an explicit design invariant.

ALREADY DONE (self-admitted). The candidate text itself says 'COMPLETED positive-impact change … No further optimization needed here.' Confirmed at model_stage_decoder_tc 1715-1727: the single-owner grid-stride column-sum is already in place ('WAS: each CTA strided ALL bias outputs … this task set out to fix'). Reference-only, no action.

FALSE PREMISE. Claims ViT P2 dW uses q.next_block() atomicAdd work-steal with contention to eliminate. Ground truth (fused_vit_megakernel 612: 'for (int item=cta; item<n_dw*kDwG; item+=nCTA)' and 619 'for (int gt=cta; gt<n_dw; gt+=nCTA)') — the ViT P2 dW ALREADY uses exactly the deterministic fixed-stride round-robin partition the candidate proposes. The optimization is already implemented.

PARTIAL-DROP (fwd-fusion half). The fwd LN mean/variance fusion claims 'bit-identical (same accumulation order)' but Σ(x-mean)² is INHERENTLY two-pass: a single-pass sum/sumsq computes var=E[x²]-E[x]² which is a DIFFERENT rounding (catastrophic-cancellation-prone) → fails fp32 bit-identity. The bwd sync-merge half is kept (model_track rank 6); only the parity-breaking fwd fusion is dropped.

SUB-NOISE + REVERSES A DELIBERATE CHOICE. Claims '2 powf per Muon optimization' done on-device. Ground truth (fused_decoder 1297-1298): a_bc1/a_bc2 are computed ONCE PER TENSOR (outside the element loop at 1299), not per element. The comment explicitly states they were 'kept out of the mirror to shrink the host ABI; fp32 powf, tol 2e-3 ample' — a deliberate ABI-shrink. ~2 powf × ~11 Muon-1D tensors = sub-noise; widening the host ABI by 2 floats to save it reverses an intentional decision.

Ground truth (opt_components 483-484): psi_b2 IS read once before the psi forward; it's a single scalar deref of loop-invariant st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden] that the compiler trivially hoists. Cannot fuse without breaking the dependency. Also GrokAdamW/NeuralGrok-only and the norm pass is one sweep over ~400K elems.

summary:
SCOPE/GROUNDING: root /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/compile.py DOES NOT EXIST — every candidate citing it (COMPILE_PY_BUILD_CACHE_HOIST, COMPILE_PY_PTXAS_INLINE_HINTS, BUILD-001/002) has a fabricated locus; the real autotuner is grokking_optimizers/compile.py and the K-loop pragmas live in the .cuh headers. I read the production GEMM core, the swizzle substrate, the P3/apply_optimizer dispatch, adamw.h, the SG2 meta-stages, and the cited compile.py loci.

96 raw → 27 kept (10 compile / 8 model / 9 optimizer), 49 dropped (incl. dedup merges). 

THREE FALSE-PREMISE THEMES drove the biggest drops: (1) SWIZZLE (WGMMA_SMEM_BANK_SWIZZLE / PERF-001 / BEHAVIOR-001) — claimed 'flip descriptor bits 63:62, zero-copy, bit-neutral,' but wgmma.cuh:250-288 derives LBO/SBO and the staging map at model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:584-594 SPECIFICALLY for the NONE/INTERLEAVE layout; 128B swizzle needs a different smem write-map + re-derived LBO/SBO or the GEMM reads garbage. Parity-risk, not free. (2) S=3 RING (RING_DEPTH_INCREASE_S3 / PERF-003) — kDecTcStages is hard static_assert'd <=2 (lines 116-117); S=3 is a ring rewrite, not a tunable bump. (3) ALREADY-DONE / FALSE-PREMISE — PERF-006 bias grid-stride is self-admittedly complete (1715-1727); VIT_TC_012 claims an atomicAdd work-steal to remove but fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:612 ALREADY uses the proposed deterministic round-robin. LAUNCH_BOUNDS_OCCUPANCY_TUNING contradicts the persistent one-CTA-per-SM GridBarrier invariant (occ>=1 assert, 42KB smem). VIT_TC_002's fwd-LN fusion was split: the bwd-sync-merge survives, the fwd Σ(x-mean)² single-pass is dropped (inherently two-pass; bit-identity unachievable).

FLAGSHIPS (one per track):
- MODEL → PERF-004 Split-K dW increase (4→8): bit-NEUTRAL by construction (deterministic ascending-chunk reduce, 1576-1592), attacks the single largest documented d=2048 inefficiency (~62% idle SMs in P2 dW), gated only by a clean tunable bump (kDecDwSplitK has NO blocking assert, only >=1) + workspace-headroom check. Highest gain×confidence/risk in the entire set.
- OPTIMIZER → elemwise-001 vec4 AdamW: the float4 fast-path is ALREADY WRITTEN (adamw.h:65-105) but never called — the P3 loop (fused_decoder:288) runs scalar. Lowest-effort/highest-certainty, bit-identical, bites on the large ff0/ff2 tensors at d=2048.
